old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-h3lm","title":"Gateway HAT/serial ingress bypasses link signature and replay verification","description":"P1 security review finding. rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs run_hat_inner(), run_serial(), and run_sim() pass received bytes directly to forward_mesh_to_upstream(); that function calls Gateway::process_rpl() and Gateway::mesh_to_upstream() on the bare buffer. rust/lichen-gateway/src/lib.rs mesh_to_upstream() directly SCHC-decompresses the buffer and emits IPv6 toward the upstream TUN, while process_rpl() parses route-control traffic; neither path calls LinkLayer::receive_frame() nor requires opaque link-auth/replay/destination evidence. A direct SX1302 HAT receive is an on-air payload, so an attacker can inject arbitrary unsigned/spoofed SCHC IPv6 into the TUN (and separately attempt RPL mutation); valid signed LICHEN frames are not parsed at this boundary either. Require exact link-frame parsing, signature/key-pin/generation/replay verification, and destination admission before SCHC/RPL processing, with authenticated evidence threaded through APIs. If a serial transport delegates authentication, define an authenticated envelope carrying peer and replay evidence rather than accepting bare bytes. Add negative tests proving unsigned, bad-signature, replayed, and foreign-destination frames cannot affect TUN output or routing state.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"me@mark.atwood.name","created_at":"2026-08-24T12:25:22.158854Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-08-24T12:25:22.158854Z"}
